reference.title: Dumbbell Plyo Squat
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in on the way down, brace, breathe out sharply on the jump; breathe again once landed and stable.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short pause, explosive jump, soft landing

prescription.tempo: Controlled down, explosive up, soft landing
prescription.frequency: 1-2 times a week, not on consecutive days
prescription.progression: More height before more load; keep the dumbbells light (power work). Load is user-chosen: stop the set when jump height or landing quality drops.

cues.text: Feet hip width, a light dumbbell in each hand at the sides, palms in, arms long.
Breathe in, brace and squat down, knees over the toes, chest up.
Thighs near parallel, heels down; a short pause, no bounce.
Jump: drive the floor away, extend hips, knees and ankles together; breathe out.
Legs long, toes pointed, dumbbells still at the sides.
Land softly on the balls of the feet, roll to the heels and sink into a quarter squat, knees over the toes.
Stand tall, reset the brace, repeat.

mistakes.fix: Land on the balls of the feet and bend hips and knees to absorb the landing quietly.

mistakes.mistake: Knees caving inward on take-off or landing
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees over the second toe; land with the feet hip width.
Arms stay long at the sides; the legs make the jump.
Use light dumbbells; if the jump gets lower, the load is too heavy.

kinematics.norm: A counter-movement to about 90-100 degrees of knee flexion is typical before a loaded squat jump (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Feet 14.6 cm off the floor at the top, ≈0.31 s in the air
kinematics.norm: Hips, knees and ankles extend together at take-off (triple extension; Mancini 2022 measured vertical jump and landing kinematics)

kinematics.peak: Balls of the feet first, then heels; absorbs to ≈58° knee flexion, knees over the toes
kinematics.norm: Soft landing with hip and knee flexion and the knees over the toes; instruction improves landing kinematics (Etnoyer 2013)
Leaning forward in the counter-movement, upright in the air (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Hanging at the sides, palms in
kinematics.peak: Stay at the sides (≥1.38 cm from the legs on the rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Light, hanging at the sides (common coaching)

kinematics.peak: 1.25 s down, 0.2 s pause, 0.37 s drive, flight, landing absorbed over about 0.4 s, 1.05 s back to standing

sources.title: GymVisual #2943, Dumbbell Plyo Squat, video (movement reference)
Mancini et al. 2022, Soccer-specific vertical jump and landing kinematics (Sports Med Health Sci)
Etnoyer et al. 2013, Instruction and jump-landing kinematics in college-aged female athletes (J Athl Train)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Jump on a firm, non-slip surface with space around you.
Keep the dumbbells light; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee or ankle discomfort: smaller jumps, or bodyweight squat jumps.
New to jumping: practise the landing first (drop into a quarter squat from the toes).
regressions: Dumbbell squat with a fast rise onto the toes (no flight).
progressions: Continuous jumps with a short ground contact.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Drive the jump by extending the knees fast, then work eccentrically to absorb the landing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hips explosively in the take-off and controls hip flexion on landing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Finish the take-off by pointing the feet (the last part of the triple extension) and take the first impact on the balls of the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension in the drive and co-contract to steady the knee on landing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Assist hip extension out of the bottom and keep the knees in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back flat while the trunk leans into the squat and on landing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees from caving in on take-off and landing (clinical opinion; Etnoyer 2013 on landing alignment).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbells through the jump and the landing jolt (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders steady against the dumbbells, especially on landing (clinical opinion).
